_about: Calibrated on 652 WASAC meter photos (536 readable, 98 unreadable, 17 unlabelled; 1 too large to decode), 1132 background patches and 50 COCO images. Full tables: docs/calibration/guidance_calibration.md. A null threshold turns that check off. Keys ending in _note explain each value and are ignored by the code.

yolo.guide_imgsz_note: CALIBRATED: 416 and 320 flag 5.4% and 11.5% of real meters as NO_METER (640: 2.4%), missing the 97% target, for only ~120 / ~190 ms less per frame.

checks.no_meter_window_conf_note: CALIBRATED: highest value keeping >= 97% of real meters (flags 2.7% in /submit-photo, 2.4% in frames). Non-meters passing as a meter: patches 0.5%, COCO 0% (frames 4%). Higher values only flag more meters.
checks.no_meter_min_digit_boxes_note: Spec value; with the window threshold above it meets the 97% target.
checks.too_far_min_width_frac_note: PROVISIONAL: fires on 6.7% readable vs 8.2% unreadable photos; the labels do not capture distance, so the data cannot validate it. Keep as a soft hint.
checks.cut_off_edge_frac_note: PROVISIONAL: fires on ~1% of meter photos in both groups; too rare in the data to validate. Keep as a soft hint.
checks.too_dark_max_mean_note: PROVISIONAL: fires on 0.6% readable, 0% unreadable; the photo set has almost no dark photos. Keep as a soft hint.
checks.glare_max_frac_note: PROVISIONAL, raised from 0.05: no value separates readable from unreadable (0.1 -> 4.7% vs 7.1%); 0.1 halves how often good photos are told about glare. Use a soft message.
checks.blurry_max_laplacian_var_note: OFF (calibrated decision): at every useful threshold it fires MORE on readable than unreadable photos (e.g. 80 -> 39% vs 26%), because dirty glass adds texture. Needs a better blur measure before it is used.
checks.hard_to_read_threshold_note: CALIBRATED: fires on 8.4% readable vs 83.7% unreadable (model default 0.43 -> 12.5% vs 88.8%, above the 10% nag limit). Optimistic: the unreadable photos were quality-gate training negatives.
checks.check_numbers_min_confidence_note: CALIBRATED: fires on 9.7% readable vs 32.7% unreadable (0.6 -> 26% vs 50%). Optimistic: the readable photos are the reader's training labels.
